model_annotation: This bar chart compares the "effect" values across nine linguistic families—IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic—for six different language model variants: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The horizontal axis lists the linguistic families in left-to-right order, while the vertical axis represents the "effect" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each linguistic family has a group of six bars, one for each model variant, with error bars indicating variability or confidence intervals. The bars are generally sorted by model type within each group, and their heights vary significantly across families and models. For example, in the IE-Indic family, mBERT-R₂ (light green) reaches approximately 20, XLM-R₂ (dark green) is around 18, and mBERT-B₂ (light pink) and XLM-B₂ (dark red) are both near 23–24. In contrast, the Uralic family shows very low effect values for all models, mostly near 0. The Semitic family exhibits high variability, with XLM-B₂ (dark red) reaching approximately 20 and mBERT-B₂ (light pink) around 15, while mBERT-R₂ (light green) is near 0. The Isolate family shows minimal effects across all models, with most bars near or below 1. The chart visually highlights differences in model performance or effect across language families, with IE-Indic and Semitic showing the most pronounced effects, and Uralic and Isolate showing the least.
